meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, and kids draft in one place and paste into another. Did anyone ask Owen about this before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine, he can bring it. Whatever happens here, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A seventeen-year-old got a quotation wrong, or pulled it from a different scene or a different edition. And you've stepped past my question twice, so I'm taking it that nobody spoke to Owen first.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. It's not in the scene. Is anything on his record right now, and what exactly are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
A student changes his argument between an outline and an essay; that is what an outline is for. I asked you two things, Hale. Is anything on his record, and what are you proposing?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. In writing tonight, and it says nothing is on his record now and nothing ever goes on it.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. He'll be there. What time, and who else is in the room?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: Principal

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen under procedure 4.4, after school on Thursday the twelfth and not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on his record. I still require written confirmation that nothing is on his record now, the time of the rewrite and who will be in the room, and a plain answer on whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero was entered. You said I would have this in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero, and she still wants the written commitment tonight, confirmation that nothing is on his record now, the time and who is in the room, and an answer on whether Owen was heard before the zero. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it with time left on her clock.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its times and then met her pasting defence by inviting Owen to bring his dated draft, which gave her something specific and dated that she could check herself.
What cost ground: you stepped past her question about whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero, twice, and because she tracks procedure she took your silence as a no and carried it into her email.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the essay at 11:31 PM on Wednesday, October 28, a late October night, which is as close as evidence could come. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asks whether Owen was heard before the zero went in, answer it plainly in one sentence before you show the next document, so it does not stay open against you.
